chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Death, not humiliation; and being little (self-sufficient), not relying on others. And whoever does not get while sitting will not get by standing either. And the world has two days: one for you, and one against you; so when it is for you, do not feel proud, and when it is against you, endure it!

key_terms.التَّوَسُّلُ: Relying on others / Seeking means through others
key_terms.تَبْطَرْ: To feel proud / To be arrogant

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Al-Dahr yawman' (the world has two days) in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: This maxim, often cited in discussions of *al-waqar* (dignity) and *al-sabr* (patience), reflects the Imam’s pragmatic approach to social status, emphasizing that one should not compromise their core dignity for temporary gain. The reference to 'two days' of the world (*al-dahr yawman*) echoes the Quranic concept of alternating trials and ease, urging believers to maintain spiritual equilibrium regardless of their current fortune.
